newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firms against dollar in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firms against dollar in thin trade.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling edged higher against the dollar in thin trading on Monday, as the market experienced reduced interest from both importers and exporters, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.27 against the dollar from Friday's 55.28 while on the pound, the shilling was posted at 91.79 from 91.46.
"The morning has been very quiet. A few deals here and there, but generally trading is in very low volumes," a dealer said.
"It looks like the Christmas mood has already set in. Very small flows coming in, and moderate interbank activity," another dealer said.
One dealer said the majority of inflows were from foreign investors looking to invest in treasury bills.

Last week the shilling traded within a narrow band of 55.25/30 to the dollar. Some dealers predicted the shilling would try to break the 55.30 barrier as horticultural proceeds were expected in the market this week.
The money market was a bit tight, with most banks looking for funds. Overnight rates were quoted at 20 percent levels from Friday's 18 percent levels.
